did_you_know.text: Did you know? Esther entered the inner court of the royal palace on the third day, while the king was sitting on his royal throne opposite the entrance.
Did you know? When the king saw Esther, she found favor in his eyes. He extended the golden scepter toward her, and she touched the top of the scepter.
Did you know? The king offered Esther up to “half the kingdom” and said that her request would be granted; this expression is repeated later in the chapter.
Did you know? Instead of immediately stating her request, Esther invited the king and Haman to a banquet she had prepared.
Did you know? The king ordered them to hurry and bring Haman to the banquet, and the text emphasizes how quickly this was done.
Did you know? At the first banquet, Esther said only, “My petition and my request,” but she still did not reveal what they were.
Did you know? Esther asked the king and Haman to come to another banquet the next day, and only then promised to do as the king had said and explain her request.
Did you know? Haman left the banquet joyful and in high spirits, but became very angry when he saw that Mordecai neither rose nor moved for him at the king’s gate.

Did you know? Although Haman listed his wealth, his sons, his honor, and his position, he admitted that none of these meant anything to him as long as he saw Mordecai the Jew sitting at the king’s gate.
Did you know? Zeresh and Haman’s friends suggested preparing a gallows seventy-five feet high and asking the king to hang Mordecai on it; Haman accepted their advice and prepared the gallows.
